It's clean and with English speaking and well-educated staff which is really helpful in a city where not many people speak English.

listings.name: Hotel España
listings.content: Traditional hotel with wide range of accommodation options. Lots of rooms including dorms starting at 18 soles/night, although prices for all rooms have almost doubled in the past year. Internet cafe and travel help on site. Rooms a bit outdated at times but decorated with paintings, a minimal amount of furniture and the occasional Greek statue. This family run hotel/hostel is full of greenery and generally has guests from all over the world. The restaurant serves only breakfast which can be inconvenient if you want to sit anywhere outside your room after 11:00. The crowd of guests is a great mix of different cultures and backgrounds. It can get a bit noisy with traffic around the downtown area and the constant bird noise from the two parrots who live in the rooftop courtyard. The wifi is unreliable and only reaches a few rooms.

One block from Arequipa, the boulevard that runs between downtown and San Isidro/Miraflores. A large supermarket, cinemas, bars and restaurants are a few blocks away. Clean, modern rooms with cable TV, WiFi, etc available for S/40.

Monkey islands, big cat enclosures, a large walk through aviary, penguin pools with underwater windows and bridges above. For an extra S/3 (children S/2) walk through the time tunnel to the land of dinosaurs.

Cajamarquilla
listings.content: A pre-Hispanic city covering an area of 6 km². Cajamarquilla is considered to be the second largest adobe city in Peru. The surrounding area is industrial, dusty and dirty. The site is littered with garbage. There is a security guard on a motorbike onsite for your safety and the safety of the ruins. A central plaza has been restored and excavations are taking place around the site. There are hundreds of crumbling walls, rooms, doorways, enough to keep you occupied for quite some time. Located 10km east of Lima, just off Carretera Central. It is about 5 km north from el Parque Zoológico de Huachipa. If travelling by bus take the Luringancho bus or the Ate Vitarta and then change buses. Tours can be organised from Ate Vitarte

listings.name: Cruise
listings.content: To Islas Palomino (Palomino Islands are located at short distance from the port of Lima, Callao. These small islands are inhabited by small colonies of sea lions, Peruvian boobies and Guanay cormorants. This is a reasonable alternative excursion to the famous Ballestas Islands in Paracas if you are spending some days in Lima and can not travel south to Pisco and Paracas, and also if you want to swim with the sea lions. (In Ballestas that is forbidden.) Tickets are available at the port for S/100 (March 2011) including a swim with the sea lions and a lunch or for S/70 (March 2011) (on the other corner of the square) for a round trip with the boat.

listings.name: Surfing

listings.content: TV, kitchen, minibar.

listings.name: Iglesia Matriz
listings.content: This temple is the work of the architect Ricardo Malachowski and was completed in 1930. It has a neo-colonial style façade. It is decorated with a series of stained glass windows alluding to the life of Christ.

listings.name: La Tarumba
listings.content: Circus group with headquarters in Miraflores but they do shows all over Lima, check their website for details.

listings.name: Luis Miro Quesada Garland Hall
listings.content: One of the most popular art galleries in Lima. The exhibition rooms are spacious, and the exhibitions themselves are generally very good. Work on show is mainly by local artists, with the occasional foreign contribution. Artists who display their work here usually go on to acquire a good reputation in the national art scene. Calle Virgen Milagrosa, also known as Paseo de los Pintores, often has art on display and for sale in the street.
listings.address: Municipality building, corner of calle Virgen Milagrosa and avenida Larco, opposite Parque Central

listings.name: Parque John. F. Kennedy
listings.content: Kennedy Park, also known as the Cat Park, is famous for the many cats that reside there. You can also get amazing Picarones in Kennedy Park and on the weekends they do Salsa lessons in the park that are mostly attended by seniors. If you walk by, chances are you'll get invited. The park is right at the center of the Miraflores nightlife, with fast food places, a cinema and many bars.

listings.name: Pucllana
listings.content: Huaca Pucllana dates back to 200-700 AD. Made from small handmade, sun-dried brick, this huge construction is 22 m high. It is divided into two areas, for ceremonial and administrative ends. Guided tours include a visit through the museum, the small park with native flora and fauna and the craftsmen's house where handicrafts are on exhibit and for sale. There is also a restaurant on the site itself which although expensive offers stunning views of the complex, particularly at night, when it's floodlit.

listings.name: Centro Cultural de la Universidad Cayetano Heredia
Centro Cultural de la Municipalidad de Miraflores
listings.address: Corner of Larco and Diez Canseco

listings.name: Museo Amano
listings.content: Showcases Peruvian textiles.

listings.name: Fly Adventure
listings.content: Tandem flights for a duration of about 10 minutes. There are also courses available and locations other than Miraflores.

listings.name: AeroXtreme
listings.content: Tandem flights over Miraflores, one day courses at Lurín.

listings.name: PeryFly
listings.content: Paragliding and hang gliding.

listings.name: Infinity Paragliding School
listings.content: Paragliding and hang gliding.

listings.name: Parapente Paragliding Peru
listings.content: Paragliding and hang gliding.

listings.name: Team Surf Peru
listings.content: One of the many surfschools on Makaha beach.
listings.address: Mahaka Beach, Via de las Playas

listings.name: Skate Park
listings.content: A few pipes, a bowl and some other stuff.

listings.name: BMX and Mountain Bike Track
listings.content: A dirt track with jumps.

listings.name: EDO sushi bar
listings.content: In Miraflores, San Borja and San Isidro.

listings.name: GianFranco Caffe
listings.content: Cafe with delicious ice-cream and excellent Italian pizza. A great meeting place for Italian citizens.

listings.name: La Lucha Sangucheria
listings.content: A well-established sandwich place with good juice.

listings.name: Te Burbuja
listings.content: A small Taiwanese joint close to Parque Kenedy, with nice fruit salads, all sorts of bubble tea, fruit juices and shakes.

listings.name: Fuzions
listings.content: Peruvian cuisine. This low-budget restaurant just off Larco Street is pretty basic but has tasty food and is visited mostly by locals. Ask for the menu.

listings.name: El Estragon
listings.content: Low-budget Peruvian cuisine. This restaurant serves basic but tasty Peruvian cuisine at a reasonable price. Ask for the menu.

listings.name: Mama Olla Restaurant
listings.content: Peruvian cuisine - tasty food, great pisco sours, nice service.

listings.name: Punto Azul
listings.content: Peruvian cuisine. Nice spot to try Peruvian food. Recommendation is "Piqueo Azul.

listings.name: Tanta
listings.content: Peruvian cuisine.

listings.name: Tierra Santa
listings.content: Kebab, hummus and other Turkish specialties. They have an area where you can smoke waterpipe.

listings.name: Rustica
listings.content: Pizza & parilla.

listings.name: Bembos
listings.content: Bembos is the Peruvian version of McDonald's. They add avocado and banana to some burgers. It's really good.

listings.name: Alfresco
listings.content: serving "Lima's best cerviche" for around S/30. A delightful, upmarket restaurant.

listings.name: Costanera 700
listings.content: Owner chef Sato. One of the best restaurants in Lima whose chef was once the personal chef to former Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori. Close to the beach and excellent, excellent food. Pass on the Pulpo a la oliva (unless you like your squid in black olive sauce). Try the famous Tiradito Costanera (raw fish slides in lemon juice) or Chita a la Pimienta (fish on pepper).

listings.name: La Gloria
listings.content: Mediterranean/Peruvian fine dining.

listings.name: La Rosa Nautica
listings.content: Built over the ocean beneath Larcomar, it may be one of the best restaurants in Lima. Although quite expensive, the ambience and cuisine are superb. The entree "La Rosa Nautica Style" comes highly recommended.

listings.name: Las Brujas de Cachiche
listings.content: Very good traditional Peruvian dishes.

listings.name: La Trattoria de Mambrino
listings.content: Italian restaurant.
listings.address: Av. Malecón de la Reserva 610, Int. 102

listings.name: Mangos
listings.content: Peruvian seafood. This restaurant in shopping center Larcomar has amazing views over the Pacific Ocean and serves a good Ceviche mixto.

listings.name: Rafael
listings.content: Peruvian fusion/haute-cuisine. Try the Lomo Saltado.

listings.name: Café de la Paz
listings.content: Is another excellent choice, right in front of the Kennedy Park. Peruvian-French food, in a very trendy, bohemian atmosphere. Excellent Pisco Sour.

listings.name: Downtown
listings.content: This gay club, nicknamed Vale Todo ("anything goes") lies in the heart of Miraflores and is usually one of the last clubs to close in Lima.
listings.price: S/50 to get in. Some days of the week it's free entrance

listings.name: Coffee time Miraflores
listings.content: Handmade Peruvian coffee.

listings.name: La Postreria Café
listings.content: Coffee and sandwiches

listings.name: Arabica
listings.content: They have excellent premium Peruvian coffee.

listings.name: Cirque Hostel
listings.content: Cirque is a small but cozy 6-room hostel. Free breakfast and wifi, kitchen, three common areas (TV-room, terrace, and garden), bar, airport pick-up, 24-hour hot showers and reception, as well as safety lockers and bikes for rent. The hostel is a few blocks away from the beach, local food markets and Huaca Pucllana ruins. It is also the only hostel in Lima officially providing a camping site. You can pitch your tent in the garden for S/5, facilities use will cost you extra S/5 if required.

listings.name: Pariwana Backpacker Hostel
listings.content: Hostel in front of the main Miraflores park, with a great view. 24 hours reception, bilingual staff, full guest kitchen, comfortable common areas, free breakfast, TV room, free internet and WiFi, security lockers with built-in electronic outlets, surfboard and bike rentals.

listings.name: Pirwa Hostel
listings.content: Good location in Miraflores. Comfortable beds, free breakfast, and a nice relaxing garden.

listings.name: 151 Backpackers Hostel B&B
listings.content: Fully renovated 1920s house. Private rooms, mixed dorms, outdoor patio with grill, full kitchen for your use, internet, TV and comfortable couches and living room area.

listings.name: Red Llama Eco Hostel
listings.content: At Red Psycho Llama they follow sustainable practices throughout the hotel, and guests can hang out on the rooftop patio.

listings.name: Casa del Mochilero
listings.content: This place is more like a flat than a hostel, so it has a much more at-home and chilled atmosphere, with less than 20 beds. Was the original copied by "Mochilero Inn" next door, even down to the flags outside. Dorms from S/15, one private room with two beds. Kitchen, cable TV, internet S/2 per hour.

listings.name: Flying Dog Hostel
listings.content: Spacious rooms, TV lounge with DVD selection, internet, kitchen to use, friendly English-speaking Peruvian employees. Excellent doubles with private bathroom.

listings.name: Loki Backpackers Hostel
listings.content: Loki Lima is it in the heart of Miraflores, between the buzz of Parque Kennedy and the beautiful cliff top parks of the coast. This residence is decorated with a modern Loki twist around a laid back, fun atmosphere.

listings.name: Kokopelli Backpackers Hostel
listings.content: Kokopelli was founded and run by 4 guys from Holland and Peru. Great bar on the roof, and a nice hangout area downstairs. Close to most things in Miraflores, and not a far walk to the sea. Multilingual, friendly staff. Big storage lockers, and clean rooms. Great breakfast provided at a cafe around the corner. Hot showers.
listings.price: From S/41 per person in 8-bed dorm to S/65 per person in double room.

listings.name: Thunderbird Hotel Suites & Casino
listings.content: Adjacent you will find Fiesta Casino Benavides, a quality establishment with 3 floors of gaming space and nightly live entertainment.

listings.name: Museo Aeronáutico
listings.address: Base Aérea Las Palmas, Santiago de Surco

listings.name: Museo de Historia Natural de la PUCP
Museo de Oro del Perú y Armas del Mundo
listings.content: Peru's gold museum contains a huge collection of gaudy, gold works. Not the best place to learn about Peruvian precolumbian cultures. A large part of a Peruvian 20,000-piece collection of gold is fake, according to the Peru's consumer protection agency. A new "branch office" has opened in LarcoMar in Miraflores that is much more focused and beautifully presented; best of all, of course, is that it is located in the main tourist area.
listings.address: Alonso de Molina 1100, Monterrico, Santiago de Surco (enter cdra 18 y 19 Av. Primavera)

listings.name: Los Pantanos de Villa
listings.content: 263 hectares of wetlands. 210 species of birds, 10 species of fish and some reptiles and rodents.
listings.address: Av. Hernando de Lavalle km 20, Chorrillos
listings.image: 2014 view of Laguna Principal, Refugio de Vida Silvestre los Pantanos de Villa.jpg

listings.name: La Granja Villa Sur
listings.content: A variety of animals and amusement rides. Parrots, snakes, fish, monkeys, goats, llamas, sheep, cows, pigs and more. Viking ship, bumper cars, water slide, etc. There are amusements for very small children and some even adults will find fun. Entry price includes all amusement rides. Feed for animals can be purchased for a small fee.
listings.address: Av. Alameda del Premio Real 397, Los Huertos de Villa - Chorrillos

listings.name: Biblioteca Nacional del Perú
listings.address: Av. De la Poesía 160, San Borja

listings.name: Museo de la Nacion
listings.content: The fifth floor contains an interesting photographic display detailing Peru's struggle during the years of the Shining Path.
listings.address: Av. Javier Prado Este 2465, San Borja.

listings.name: Pachacámac
listings.content: Pachacámac is about 25 km south of Lima. It is a huge archaeological site containing pre-Inca and Inca temples (entrance fee 6 Soles). This was one of the major pilgrimage sites in South America, in the years 500-1,500. The temples are constructed from adobe and are not very well preserved. There are three ramp pyramids and a temple of the sun (the only temple which may be accessed). Due to the fragile nature of the ruins and vandalism they may only be seen from a road. The on-site museum contains a variety of artifacts including ceramics, wood carvings, textiles and Inca quipus. From Miraflores, take a colectivo to 'Puente Primavera'. From there, take a 'San Bartolo' colectivo to Lurin (S/2.50). Get off just past the Cementerio Parque Del Recuerdo or tell the conductor that you want to get off at the ruinas de Pachacámac. Many bike tour companies offer tours of Pachacámac.

listings.name: Museo de Criminalística de la Policía Nacional del Perú
Hacienda Mamacona
listings.content: Hacienda Mamacona is located next to the ruins of Pachacámac and can be seen from the Temple of the Sun. Hacienda Mamacona is open to the public and is home to some of Peru's finest Paso Horses and hosts numerous events including the Festival del Caballo de Paso Peruano and Concurso Nacional del Caballo de Paso.

listings.name: Hipodromo de Monterrico
listings.content: Horse racing. Two main racetracks, one dirt and one turf. Live racing each Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday (208 race days per year, 10 races per day).
listings.address: Av. El Derby s/n, puerta 3, Santiago de Surco

listings.name: Los Inkas Golf Club
listings.content: 18-hole golf course, tennis, gymnasium, swimming pool, restaurant, cocktail lounge.
listings.address: Av. Circunvalación del Club Golf los Incas 950 Monterrico

listings.name: Country Club de Villa
listings.content: 18-hole golf course, tennis, squash, gymnasium, minigolf, soccer and fulbito (miniature soccer), Olympic swimming pool and two smaller pools, basketball, skate ramps, restaurant, bar, kids play area.

listings.name: Sanguchon Campesino Alfredo Benavides
listings.content: They have really good and greasy hamburgers, tacos, quesadillas, etc. Their best burger is probably the 'A Lo Pobre' that has burger, egg and baked banana for around S/12 and is sure to fill your stomach.
listings.address: Av. Alfredo Benavides 3580, Urb. Ovalo Higuereta

listings.name: Don Rosalino
listings.content: Italiana

listings.name: Don Tito
listings.content: Pollo a la Brasa, Parrillas, Especialidad en Carnes. You can get a Parrilla feast that feeds about 4 people for S/90 and that includes a bottle of wine.

listings.name: El Aguajal
listings.address: Av. San Borja Norte 886, San Borja

listings.name: El Characato de Oro
listings.content: Picantería

listings.name: El Huarike
listings.content: Fish and seafood.
listings.address: Av. San Borja Norte 401, San Borja

listings.name: Gian & Marco Carnes
listings.content: Steaks and grills.

listings.name: José Antonio
listings.content: Criolla

listings.name: Los Cantaritos
listings.content: Criolla
listings.address: Agustín de la Rosa Toro 1063, San Borja

listings.name: Hotel Britania
listings.content: Single, double, triple and executive suites. Restaurant, bar, gymnasium, jacuzzi and sauna
listings.address: Av. San Borja Sur 653, San Borja

listings.name: Hotel Las Lomas
listings.address: Av. San Borja Sur 585, San Borja

listings.name: Hotel Los Tulipanes
listings.address: Jr. Mercator 414 (Calle 32) Urb. Córpac, San Borja

listings.name: Hostal Paseo Norte
listings.address: Av. San Borja Norte 609, San Borja

listings.name: Hotel Rosa Toro
listings.content: Bar, restaurant, Internet, telephone, car park, bathrooms with spa, hot water.
listings.address: Av. Agustin de la Rosa Toro 1095, Urb Jacarandá, San Borja

listings.name: Hostal San Borja
listings.content: TV, Internet, air conditioning
listings.address: Morelli 316 - Cuadra 21 de Javier Prado, San Borja

listings.name: Palmetto Hotel
listings.address: Av. San Borja Sur 415, San Borja

listings.name: Hilton Garden Inn Lima Surco
listings.content: The Hilton brand makes its presence known here in the Surco business district, with a breakfast buffet and relatively classy feel compared to some of the surrounding buildings.

listings.name: Bravo Surf Camp
listings.content: It's like the quintessential hippie/gringo surf hostel with beer pong and table tennis people and cutting loose, only it's a couple of blocks from the beach. But it's comfortable and congenial with surf breaks nearby, and you can get a breakfast plan built into your room rate.
listings.address: Jr. Bartolome Herrera #100-102 Urb. Santa Cruz, Punta Hermosa

listings.name: Bahia de Ancon
listings.content: The bay of Ancon has a group of islands (Islas Pescadores) with sea lions and birds, it's possible to organize tours of the islands. Recommended to visit between September and March as that's when the most birds are there.

listings.name: Museo del Centro de Investigación Arqueológica de Ancón
Parque Ecológico Nacional Antonio Raimondi
listings.content: 8,259 hectares on the right bank of the Panamericana Norte, in the district of Ancon.

listings.name: Cerro San Cristóbal
listings.content: The hill features a large Peruvian flag painted on its slopes and is situated just north of the Rimac river. With a summit approximately 368 meters above sea level, visitors can contemplate an incomparable landscape: the city with its high buildings, the course of the river Rimac, as well as the sea ports and districts. An observation point with an illuminated cross, a museum and a restaurant are located at the summit. Many tour companies include a visit here on their itineraries, tours can also be organised near the Plaza de Armas for S/10 or an alternative is to take a taxi.

listings.name: Museo de los Descalzos
listings.content: Tours are provided in Spanish and English (it works better if required in advance). You should ring the doorbell in case you find the museum's door closed, then a volunteer will come out to start the tour.
listings.price: Adults S/7, seniors and students S/3, children S/2
listings.address: Calle Manco Cápac 202-A, Alameda de los Descalzos, Rímac

listings.name: Museo Geológico y Paleontológico
listings.address: Av. Túpac Amaru Km. 4.5 (Universidad Nacional de Ingeniería), Rimac

listings.name: Museo Del Virreinato
listings.content: Museum is under renovation.
listings.address: Quinta de Presa, Jr. Chira s/n Rimac

listings.name: Huaca El Paraiso
listings.content: Archaeological site with a small oasis nearby.

listings.name: Petroglifos de Checta
listings.content: About 450 petroglyphs (rock carvings). Spiders, foxes, pumas, fish and more.

listings.name: La Granja Villa Norte
listings.content: Amusement Park
listings.address: Av. Condorcanqui 2751, Urb. Chacra Cerro, Comas.

listings.name: Alianza Francesa Los Olivos
listings.content: Free admission to see French/independent films at night. Also a cultural center.
listings.address: Jr. Pancho Fierro 3498, Urb. Panamericana Norte, Los Olivos

listings.name: Británico Los Jardines
listings.content: British cultural center with free entrance to general activities. The entire building is under renovation.
listings.address: Av. Alfredo Mendiola 1200, Los Jardines, San Martín de Porres

listings.name: Teatro UNI
listings.content: Sometimes, free music concerts and lectures (in Spanish). It´s located in the campus of a university (UNI).

listings.name: La Barra de Chiki Cevichería Resto-Bar
listings.content: Local cevichería and resto-bar serving Peruvian seafood and criollo dishes. Specialties include cevi-pato (ceviche served with arroz con pato). Offers dine-in, takeaway, delivery, and reservations.

listings.name: Las Brisas
listings.address: Mza. D Lote 11 Urb. Garcilazo De La Vega (Frente Parroquia Virgen Del Rosario)

listings.name: Calin Hostal
listings.address: Av. Juan Velasco Alvarado Mz. I Lt. 6 Urb. Virgen Del Rosario (Alt . Parque Del Rosario)

listings.name: Hostal La Estacion
listings.address: Mza. D Lote 17 A.H. Las Esteras II

listings.name: El Paraiso
listings.address: Av. Garcilazo De La Vega Mza. S/N Lote 7 Urb. Garcilazo De La Vega

listings.name: La Casa del Turista
listings.content: If you don't mind enamoring yourself with the local scene and with a local friendly host, this small inn could be quite a pleasant experience. Dining available. You are predisposed to get a glimpse of real Limeno life here, including with a chifa restaurant just steps away.

listings.name: Mama Backpackers Hostel
listings.content: Hot showers, complimentary breakfast, welcoming host found here.
listings.address: Av. Antunez de Mayolo 1389, Los Olivos

listings.name: Tampu Machi Hostel
listings.content: This is a cheapie but still a good hostel in which to stay, with a large quantity of offerings such as eggs for breakfast.
